original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-hom}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$
be differential graded algebras over $R$. Let $N$ be a
differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule. The construction above
defines a functor
$$
\Hom_{\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}}(N, -) :
\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}
\longrightarrow
\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(A, \text{d})}
$$
of differential graded categories. This functor induces functors
$$
\text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})} \to \text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}
\quad\text{and}\quad
K(\text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})}) \to K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})
$$
by an application of Lemma \ref{lemma-functorial}.

statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$
be differential graded algebras over $R$. Let $N$ be a
differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule. The dg Hom construction $M\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_B(N,M)$ with its induced dg $A$-action
defines a functor
$$
\Hom_{\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}}(N, -) :
\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}
\longrightarrow
\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(A, \text{d})}
$$
of differential graded categories. This functor induces functors
$$
\text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})} \to \text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}
\quad\text{and}\quad
K(\text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})}) \to K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})
$$ by passing to closed degree-zero maps and homotopy classes.
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring; A and B are dg R-algebras; N is a dg (A,B)-bimodule.
conclusions: The internal Hom functor Hom_B(N,-) defines a dg functor from dg right B-modules to dg right A-modules, and induces functors on ordinary dg-module and homotopy categories.
